name: O2C baseline
description: Order-to-cash norm derived from the failure-mode catalogue of the o2c pack. Activity parameters are canonical ids (o2c.*) translated through the activity mapping; return items and items rejected at capture are excluded from delivery-performance constraints by applicability rules; open items are scored by their age (lag with missing_b = censor). Every threshold is a placeholder flagged uncalibrated in metadata.meta.

case_attributes.return_item: Returns Item (X for return items) in the hackathon extract
case_attributes.days_late: goods issue date minus requested delivery date in days; prepared before scoring
case_attributes.flow_type: derived by recipe from planning type, partial delivery indicator, return flag and rejection status

notes: Measured shares of the hackathon extract (o2c/README.md) are seeds for the catalogue, not thresholds.
Make-to-order items need their own order-to-issue threshold; restrict o_deliv_order_to_issue_days by flow_type once planning types are known.
The balance constraint is always satisfied on the hackathon extract because confirmed quantity equals ordered quantity for every item.

guidance.source: guidance.yaml of the pack (generic tier); the project overlay is stored with the project

capture.expectation: Orders are captured for customers whose credit is in order, so that a credit block is the exception and, when it happens, is released within a day or two.
capture.meaning_when_missed: The order was held at capture because the customer's credit limit or overdue receivables stopped it, or the block stayed on the order for days before someone released it.
capture.why_it_matters: Every blocked order waits for a decision that involves credit management, sales and the customer; confirmed dates slip while it waits, and the customer hears about it late or not at all.
capture.how_detected: Two expectations: no credit block on the item, and a credit block released within a target of one day with a tolerance of three; blocks still open at the end of the data are scored by their age. The hackathon extract has no credit events, so both stay vocabulary there.

usual_reasons.text: The customer's credit limit is exhausted by open receivables or overdue invoices
usual_reasons.check: share of blocked items per customer against the customer's open receivables and dunning level at the time of the block, where the receivables log is joined

usual_reasons.text: Credit master data is outdated (limit, risk class) although the customer pays on time
usual_reasons.check: ask credit management which blocked customers had no overdue item at the time of the block

usual_reasons.text: The automatic credit check is set too strict for the order value distribution
usual_reasons.check: ask credit management for the check settings (static or dynamic, horizon) and compare them with the order value bands

usual_actions.text: Credit limit review cadence per customer group with a rule for temporary limit increases
Dunning before the limit is reached, so that receivables and not the order desk absorb the problem
Credit master data (limit, risk class) maintained with finance on a fixed schedule

what_to_check_first: Whether credit events are logged at all for this sales organisation
Customers with the most blocks and their receivables at the time
How long blocks stay open and who releases them

examples.text: An order item blocked at capture for a customer with two overdue invoices, released four days later after the customer paid.
An order item captured without a block and confirmed the same day.

commitment.expectation: Once a quantity and a date are confirmed to the customer they hold: no postponement, no withdrawn confirmation, no cancellation after confirmation, no delivery block, no stock-out, and the confirmed quantity equals the ordered one.
commitment.meaning_when_missed: The customer was told a date or a quantity that later changed: the scheduled date was pushed out, the confirmed quantity was removed or cut, the item was cancelled after it had been confirmed, or a block or a stock-out interrupted it.
commitment.why_it_matters: A broken promise costs more than a late one: the customer plans on the confirmation, and every change triggers calls, re-planning on both sides and, in the extract, cancellations that follow postponements.
commitment.how_detected: Exclusion expectations on the postponement, confirmation-removal, rejection, block and stock-out events, and a balance expectation comparing the confirmed with the ordered quantity at item creation; return items and items rejected at capture are out of scope. In the extract 3.2 % of items were postponed, 1.5 % had a confirmation removed and 2.8 % were cancelled according to the customer.

usual_reasons.text: Material availability changed after the availability check (supply or production slipped)
usual_reasons.check: share of postponed items with an availability-date change on the same item; SKU and plant concentration

usual_reasons.text: A supplier delay on the purchase side of the same SKU
usual_reasons.check: purchase-order confirmation changes for the SKU in the same period (purchase extract)

usual_reasons.text: Backorder processing reallocated confirmed stock to another order
usual_reasons.check: confirmation removals clustered on rescheduling run dates; a new confirmation following the removal

usual_reasons.text: The customer asked for a later date or cancelled (legitimate; the change is theirs)
usual_reasons.check: changed_from and changed_to values and the rejection reason code (80 cancelled according to customer, 82 double order, 99 handling error)

usual_reasons.text: Confirmations are given from planned receipts instead of stock
usual_reasons.check: ask supply planning how the availability check is configured (stock only, planned receipts, replenishment lead time)

usual_actions.text: Confirm from stock or from firm supplier confirmations only; date tolerance in the availability check
Allocation rules that protect confirmed quantities; rescheduling only with sales approval
Expedite purchase orders of SKUs with repeated postponements; safety stock review per planning type
Record the reason for every date move, so that customer-requested moves can be excluded from the reading

Whether cancellations follow postponements on the same items
Whether the moved dates were requested by the customer (changed_from and changed_to)

delivery.missed_label: shipped late, split or not at all
delivery.missed_label_de: zu spät, geteilt oder gar nicht geliefert
delivery.expectation: Every deliverable item gets a delivery and a goods issue, ships within the target time and not later than the requested date, leaves within a day of picking, in one delivery unless partial deliveries are allowed, and without a failed attempt.
delivery.meaning_when_missed: The item has no delivery or goods issue, left the warehouse late or later than the customer asked, waited after picking, was split over several deliveries, or the delivery attempt failed.
delivery.why_it_matters: Delivery reliability is what the customer measures the company on; late or split shipments mean penalties, extra freight, repeated handling and backlog that sales has to explain.
delivery.how_detected: Presence expectations on the delivery and the goods issue, an order-to-issue time expectation (target 14 days, tolerance to 30; open items scored by their age), a lateness expectation on the prepared days-late attribute (target 0, tolerance 7 days), a pick-to-issue time expectation (1 day, tolerance 3), a no-split expectation on standard and make-to-order items, and no failed delivery. Return items and items rejected at capture are out of scope. In the extract 3.2 % of shipped items were late, the median order-to-issue time was 1.9 days with a p90 of 67 days, and 4.8 % of items had no goods issue at the end of the data.

usual_reasons.text: The item was still open when the data was extracted (right-censoring)
usual_reasons.check: share of items without goods issue whose creation is within the last weeks of the window; read presence shortfalls only after excluding them

usual_reasons.check: ask master data for the planning type of the long-tail SKUs; give make-to-order items their own threshold

usual_reasons.text: Picking backlog or carrier cut-offs hold picked goods
usual_reasons.check: pick-to-issue lag by plant, weekday and incoterm

usual_reasons.text: Partial availability shipped early to meet the date (split), or the customer allows partial deliveries
usual_reasons.check: ask logistics and sales which customers carry a partial-delivery indicator

usual_actions.text: Separate make-to-order planning types with their own order-to-issue threshold

Open-item review per customer with an age limit; automatic rejection of dead items after an agreed age
Ship-complete indicator per customer and consolidation rules

changes.expectation: An order item is captured right the first time and then changed rarely: at most one change event, at most one availability-date move, at most one date move forward, and no requested-quantity change after capture.
changes.meaning_when_missed: The item was touched again and again after capture: dates oscillated, the availability date was rescheduled repeatedly, or the requested quantity was corrected.
changes.why_it_matters: Every change is work for the order desk and planning, a new confirmation to the customer, and a sign that either the capture or the planning parameters are unstable; in the extract 13.7 % of items carry changes, 2.3 each on average.
changes.how_detected: A metric expectation on the count of change events (target 1, tolerance to 3) and three repetition expectations: availability-date changes (more than one), date moves forward (more than one) and requested-quantity changes (any). Return items and items rejected at capture are out of scope of the count. In the extract 9.9 % of items had an availability-date change and 7.8 % a date moved forward.

usual_reasons.text: Repeated availability checks reschedule the item every time supply changes (date oscillation)
usual_reasons.check: sequence of availability-date, postpone and prepone events per item; SKU and plant concentration

usual_reasons.text: The customer changes quantity or date after capture
usual_reasons.check: requested-quantity change events and changed_from and changed_to values per customer

usual_reasons.text: Capture errors corrected by hand (wrong quantity, wrong date)
usual_reasons.check: changes within an hour of item creation

usual_reasons.text: Order-level changes replicated onto every item of the order
usual_reasons.check: identical change timestamps across the items of one order (replication diagnostic)

usual_reasons.text: Rescheduling runs during the confirmation window
usual_reasons.check: ask supply planning for the rescheduling calendar and horizon

usual_actions.text: Freeze window for schedule-line changes close to delivery; batch rescheduling outside the confirmation window
Validation of quantities and dates at order entry; templates for recurring orders
Stable planning parameters per SKU (lead time, lot size) reviewed with the material master

commercial.missed_label: terms or price changed after capture
commercial.missed_label_de: Konditionen oder Preis nach Erfassung geändert
commercial.expectation: Delivery terms and prices are what the customer agreement says, so that neither the incoterms nor the price is changed by hand after capture.
commercial.meaning_when_missed: The delivery terms were changed on the item after it was captured, or the price was overridden manually; either the master data was wrong or the terms were negotiated per order.
commercial.why_it_matters: Manual prices and per-order terms are where margin leaks and where invoice corrections start; they are commercial-risk indicators to review, not audit findings.
commercial.how_detected: Exclusion of incoterms changes and a repetition expectation on manual price changes (any). Manual price events are not in the hackathon extract; incoterms changed on 0.8 % of items there.

usual_reasons.text: The customer master carries outdated delivery terms, so the desk corrects them on every order
usual_reasons.check: incoterms changes concentrated on a few customers with the same changed_from and changed_to pair

usual_reasons.text: Terms or discounts negotiated per order instead of per customer
usual_reasons.check: ask sales which customers have per-order agreements

usual_reasons.text: Price condition records missing for the customer and material, so the price is typed in
usual_reasons.check: ask sales operations which customer and material combinations have no condition record

usual_actions.text: Incoterms and prices maintained in the customer master and condition records; a change on the order needs a reason
Approval workflow for manual discounts and term deviations above a limit
Condition maintenance cadence with the price list owner

what_to_check_first: Customer concentration of the changes and the from-to pairs
Whether invoice corrections follow on the same items
Whether the changed value matches the customer master

returns.missed_label: goods came back or the issue was reversed
returns.missed_label_de: Ware kam zurück oder Warenausgang storniert
returns.expectation: A posted goods issue is not reversed, and returns come back through a return order that exists before the goods arrive at the dock.
returns.meaning_when_missed: The goods issue was cancelled after posting, or goods came back without an authorised return order, or a return item shows no returned goods at all.
returns.why_it_matters: Reversals hide shipping errors and premature postings; unauthorised returns block the dock, delay credit memos and leave the customer without an answer.
returns.how_detected: Exclusion of goods-issue reversals on ordinary items; on return items a presence expectation on the returned goods and an order expectation that the return order precedes the return delivery (a missing return order counts as missed). The extract holds 20 return items and 397 reversal movements in the stock-movement table; the join between them was not made, so the return expectations stay vocabulary.

usual_reasons.text: The goods issue was posted before the truck left and the shipment was then cancelled
usual_reasons.check: time between issue and reversal; whether a new goods issue follows on the same item

usual_reasons.text: Wrong delivery or quantity posted and corrected by reversal
usual_reasons.check: reversals followed by a delivery change and a new issue

usual_reasons.text: Goods sent back by the customer without an authorisation
usual_reasons.check: return deliveries with no return order or with the return order created after the receipt

usual_reasons.text: The customer refused the delivery at the dock
usual_reasons.check: ask customer service which reversals were refusals and why

usual_actions.text: Goods issue posted at physical departure, with delivery checks before posting
Return authorisation before acceptance at the dock; a return portal for customers
Join return items with the returns stock movements before reading the return expectations

what_to_check_first: Time between issue and reversal and whether a new issue follows
Plant and customer concentration of reversals
Whether return orders exist before the return deliveries

examples.text: A goods issue posted on Friday and reversed on Monday because the pallet never left; issued again on Tuesday.

invoice_payment.missed_label: invoice or payment missing or late
invoice_payment.missed_label_de: Rechnung oder Zahlung fehlt oder verspätet
invoice_payment.expectation: Every shipped item is invoiced within two days of the goods issue without corrections, and every invoiced item is paid within terms without a reminder.
invoice_payment.meaning_when_missed: The shipped item has no invoice or a late one, the invoice was cancelled or corrected, the invoiced item is unpaid, paid after the due date or dunned.
invoice_payment.why_it_matters: Working capital sits in unbilled shipments and overdue receivables; corrections and reminders cost accounts receivable and the customer relationship.
invoice_payment.how_detected: Presence of the invoice on shipped items and of the payment on invoiced items, time expectations goods issue to invoice (2 days, tolerance to 5) and invoice to payment (30 days, tolerance to 60; open receivables scored by their age), exclusion of invoice corrections outside returns and of dunning. Billing and payment are not in the hackathon extract, so the whole area is vocabulary until a log covers it.

usual_reasons.text: Billing block on the item or the billing due list not processed daily
usual_reasons.check: goods issue to invoice lag by billing block and by day of month

usual_reasons.text: Order-related billing configured although a delivery exists
usual_reasons.check: ask accounts receivable which item categories bill from the order rather than the delivery

usual_reasons.text: Disputes on invoice content (price, quantity) delay the payment
usual_reasons.check: invoice corrections and manual price changes on the late-paid items

usual_reasons.text: Customer payment behaviour and lenient dunning levels
usual_reasons.check: invoice to payment days per customer against the customer's payment terms; dunning level history

usual_reasons.text: Invoice sent to the wrong address or channel
usual_reasons.check: ask accounts receivable which customers require e-invoicing or a portal

usual_actions.text: Daily billing due list run and billing block review
Dunning cadence and levels per customer group; dispute management with a clock
E-invoicing for the largest customers
Payment terms per customer as a case attribute, so that days beyond terms are scored instead of a fixed target

o_invoice_days_after_issue.expectation: The invoice follows the goods issue within two days, with a tolerance to five; unbilled items are scored by their age.
o_invoice_days_after_issue.meaning_when_missed: The billing document came days after the goods left, or has not come yet.
o_invoice_days_after_issue.why_it_matters: Every day between shipment and invoice is a day added to the cash cycle.
o_invoice_days_after_issue.how_detected: A time expectation from the goods issue to the invoice with a target of 2 days and a tolerance to 5 (placeholders, uncalibrated); unbilled items are censored and scored by their age; return items are out of scope. Vocabulary in the extract.

o_invoice_no_corrections.expectation: The invoice of an ordinary item is not cancelled, corrected or followed by a credit or debit memo.
o_invoice_no_corrections.meaning_when_missed: The invoice was wrong and had to be cancelled or corrected; credit memos on return items are legitimate and out of scope.
o_invoice_no_corrections.why_it_matters: Corrections delay payment, cost accounts receivable and point to price, quantity or master-data errors upstream.
o_invoice_no_corrections.how_detected: An exclusion expectation on the cancellation, correction request, credit memo and debit memo events on items that are not return items. Vocabulary in the extract.

o_pay_within_terms.expectation: The payment arrives within thirty days of the invoice, with a tolerance to sixty; open receivables are scored by their age.
o_pay_within_terms.meaning_when_missed: The customer paid late or has not paid yet.
o_pay_within_terms.why_it_matters: Days beyond terms are working capital; the fixed target is a placeholder until payment terms per customer are a case attribute.
o_pay_within_terms.how_detected: A time expectation from the invoice to the payment with a target of 30 days and a tolerance to 60 (placeholders, uncalibrated); open receivables are censored and scored by their age. Vocabulary in the extract.

constraints.description: Credit blocks should be exceptional.
Credit blocks should be released within a target time; open blocks are scored by their age.
The committed delivery date should not be postponed.
A confirmed quantity should not be withdrawn.
Confirmed items should not be cancelled afterwards.
Delivery blocks should be exceptional.
Committed items should not run out of stock.
The confirmed quantity should equal the ordered quantity.
Deliverable items should get a delivery.
Deliverable items should be shipped.
Items should ship within a target time; open items are scored by their age.
Goods issue should not be later than the requested delivery date.
Picked goods should leave within a target time.
Items should not be split across deliveries unless partial deliveries are allowed.
Delivery attempts should not fail.
Items should not carry more than the tolerated number of change events.
Repeated availability date changes indicate planning churn.
Repeated date moves in either direction indicate unstable commitments.
Requested quantity changes after capture should be rare.
Delivery terms should not change after capture.
Manual price changes indicate commercial inconsistency risk.
Goods issues should not be reversed.
Return items should show the returned goods.
Returns should be authorised by a return order before the goods arrive.
Shipped items should be invoiced.
Invoices should follow the goods issue within a target time.
Invoice corrections should be exceptional outside returns.
Invoiced items should be paid.
Payment should arrive within terms; open receivables are scored by their age.
Payment reminders should be exceptional.
